Stars-and-bars over t+1 left gaps proves the displayed exact histogram. The smallest prime divisor p bounds t for any multi-cycle itinerary; two explicit primitive words attain and separate the sharp minima. A generating-function complement gives exact extremal counts and their polynomial asymptotic. Standard-library checker executed successfully from this package: 8,104 words and all t histograms for 2<=M<=9, 1<=n<=9; finite tests support but do not replace the analytic proof.

value.rationale: The primary paper uses lack of uniform periodic expansion as a defining feature. The earliest iterate length supporting distinct periodic eigenvalue moduli is a natural finite-scale quantitative invariant; its exact dependence on the smallest prime divisor of dimension is not a rote parameter substitution. The full exact histogram and extremal count classify all return-instability strata at every finite length, and show that the weakest multipliers are exponentially rare despite the nonuniform asymptotic infimum. These precise values support studying how periodic spectral nonuniformity emerges as dimension varies.
